items.description: The cliffs of Toco present a rugged and scenic shoreline, marking the dramatic northern tip of the island.
The beach ridges of Manzanilla create a unique coastal relief, separating the expansive beaches from the interior forests.
The Valencia Plateau is a broad, elevated landscape providing a distinct relief feature in the northeastern interior.
The hills surrounding Sangre Grande form part of the diverse and undulating topography of northeastern Trinidad.
The Mayaro lowlands encompass wide, flat coastal areas that define the southeastern geography of the island.
The valleys of Brasso are characterized by their gentle relief and fertile soil, nestled in the central hills of Trinidad.
The rugged coast of Matelot is known for its steep, dramatic relief and pristine, untamed beauty in the far north.
The hills of Tabaquite form a hilly interior region, contributing to the undulating and varied topography of central Trinidad.
